title: A Cover for the Safehouse
premise: Elodie Brightwater, a crash investigator haunted by the deaths of his family in row twelve of Flight 4471, has spent six years hiding behind a fabricated identity and a carefully polished lie about who he is. When a stranger named Marcus Vale repays a favor Elodie never performed—and demands interest—Elodie is dragged into a conspiracy surrounding the crash he's spent his career quietly investigating: the airline falsified maintenance records, and the only surviving copy is hidden in a safehouse whose location is buried in Elodie's own fractured memories of that night. As Vale's employers close in and Elodie realizes his 'memories' were partially implanted by witness protection handlers protecting him, he must choose between exposing the truth that will destroy the airline's powerful backers and preserving the last fragile version of his family that lives in what he remembers. In the end, Elodie trades the secret—handing the records to a federal prosecutor at devastating personal cost—and discovers the final memory was real after all: his daughter survived, hidden by the same people who erased him.
about_author: Petra Reyes is a former aviation safety analyst who left the industry after a decade of investigating accidents no one wanted fully explained. She writes thrillers from a coastal town she refuses to name, drawing on her insider knowledge of how institutions bury their dead twice—once in wreckage, once in paperwork.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Elodie Brightwater's POV. On the sixth anniversary of the crash, Elodie rehearses his cover story in a mirror, checks his go-bag, and attends the memorial where he must pretend to be a stranger to his own family's grief. Emotional beat: controlled grief cracking at the seams.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Was
chapters.summary: Marcus Vale appears at Elodie's office with a file of debts Elodie never incurred, thanking him for services rendered on a night Elodie cannot remember. The stranger knows details only someone from Elodie's past life could know. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath polite conversation.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. Vale reports to an unseen employer that the asset is located and responsive, revealing he was sent not to collect money but to test whether Elodie's memory has begun returning. Emotional beat: professional detachment masking unease about the job.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Following protocol drilled into him years ago, Elodie abandons his apartment and triggers a dead-drop contact protocol—but the handler who answers is someone new, and the recognition phrase fails. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing his safety net was cut long ago.

chapters.title: What the Wreckage Keeps
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Using his investigator credentials, Elodie pulls the official crash report and finds page discrepancies—maintenance logs altered between versions. A flash of memory: a hangar, rain, a man saying 'row twelve was never random.' Emotional beat: obsession igniting into purpose.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Remembers Him
chapters.summary: Dana Okafor's POV. Dana, a former NTSB colleague, recognizes Elodie at a hearing despite his changed face, and reveals he testified before the crash—not after it—and then vanished from the record. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming over shared suspicion.

chapters.title: Safehouse Protocol
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie decodes coordinates embedded in his own old habits—a route he walks without thinking leads to a boarded transit depot. Inside: a cache with documents bearing his pre-crash name and a photograph of him holding the maintenance ledger. Emotional beat: self-recognition as horror.

chapters.title: Erasure
chapters.summary: Handler POV (the new contact, Renner). Renner reviews Elodie's file: he wasn't protected after witnessing the crash—he was a whistleblower whose testimony threatened Meridian Airline's parent conglomerate, and the memory gaps were manufactured. Emotional beat: institutional evil rendered as routine paperwork.

chapters.title: Vale's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. Ordered to eliminate Elodie now that the safehouse is compromised, Vale hesitates—the favor he cited was real, owed by his employer to Elodie from a debt they've rewritten. He burns the kill order instead. Emotional beat: conscience surfacing through cynicism.

chapters.title: Two Runners
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie and Dana compare notes and realize both are being fed false memories—Dana's 'promotion' after the crash was exile. They plan to move the ledger before Renner's team sweeps the depot. Emotional beat: trust built cautiously between two broken witnesses.

chapters.title: The Sweep
chapters.summary: Renner's POV. The depot raid finds the cache empty but recovers Elodie's fingerprint trail; Renner escalates to the conglomerate's fixer, Calloway, who authorizes broader measures—including Dana. Emotional beat: machinery of violence accelerating past its operators' control.

chapters.title: Implanted
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Under stress, Elodie's memories fracture violently, and a neurologist confirms signs of deliberate hypnotic conditioning. His most cherished memory—his daughter's voice reading in row twelve—may be a constructed anchor. Emotional beat: grief weaponized against himself.

chapters.title: Calloway's Offer
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. Calloway meets Elodie openly, offering restoration of his true identity, financial security, and 'closure files' on his family—in exchange for the ledger and signed silence. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy, power corrupting through kindness.

chapters.title: The Daughter Question
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Digging into passenger manifests, Elodie finds an anomaly: seat 12F was reassigned at the gate, and a child's name was struck from the final list. Hope becomes unbearable. Emotional beat: desperate, dangerous hope.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Burned
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Dana attempts to pass the ledger copy to a journalist and walks into a trap; wounded, she stashes the documents and goes dark, leaving Elodie a coded message using their old NTSB shorthand. Emotional beat: sacrifice and betrayal of trust in institutions.

chapters.title: Vale Changes Sides
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. Ordered to finish Dana, Vale instead extracts her, choosing open rebellion against Calloway. He gives Elodie the missing piece: the ledger's second half, which names the safehouse's true contents—not just records, but a living witness list. Emotional beat: redemption through defection.

chapters.title: The Real Safehouse
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Following the witness-list thread, Elodie reaches a coastal cottage and finds a teenage girl—Mira—alive, hidden for six years under protection that Calloway's people infiltrated and corrupted. Emotional beat: overwhelming reunion shadowed by immediate danger.

chapters.title: Siege at the Cottage
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Renner's team surrounds the cottage; Vale holds the door while Elodie and Mira escape through the tidal marsh; Dana returns with the ledger to draw fire. Emotional beat: loyalty proven under fire, losses mounting.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Cornered, Elodie offers Calloway the trade he demanded—the ledger for Mira's clean escape—but delivers it simultaneously to a federal prosecutor via dead-man's switch, making the secret public the moment anything happens to any of them. Emotional beat: checkmate built on truth as leverage.

chapters.title: Collateral Reckoning
chapters.summary: Renner's POV. With the ledger public, the conglomerate cuts its losses: Renner is ordered to stand down and become the fall guy, while Calloway vanishes mid-flight—aboard a plane whose maintenance history Elodie recognizes all too well. Emotional beat: justice arriving sideways, imperfectly.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Before the federal inquiry, Elodie reconstructs his true testimony from recovered memory fragments, corroborated by Vale and Dana, dismantling the erasure program piece by piece. Emotional beat: reclamation of self through truth-telling.

chapters.title: A Cover No Longer Needed
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, epilogue. Months later, Elodie unpacks the go-bag for good, walks the memorial wall with Mira beside him, and finally grieves honestly—no cover story, no polished lie. Vale sends a postcard: no favors outstanding. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory owned at last.
